cands.bio: Democrat from Goldsboro. U.S. Army Gulf War veteran, former teacher and football coach, and transportation planner. Served on the Wayne County school board (2016–2019) and in the North Carolina House, District 21 (2019–2023). Ran for the U.S. House in District 3 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia in 2026 as endorsed or recommended by several Sway voter-guide groups, including "Reject AIPAC from City Council to Congress" (Vote for Peace), Before the Day, and Waves of Democracy.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, growth and land conservation, immigration enforcement or H-1B, abortion, or gun policy. His campaign platform covers corruption and campaign finance reform, healthcare, costs, infrastructure, veterans and public education, with no pledge to refuse particular kinds of donations. We could not read his legislative sponsorship list. The only record of his bills is a claim on his campaign site that he introduced legislation on education, community revitalization and Medicaid expansion. The pages we had give no date for when he moved to or lived elsewhere than Goldsboro, and no details on his controversies, if any.

qual.background: Two terms in the NC House (2019–2023, committees including Appropriations, Finance and Local Government). Wayne County school board member (2016–2019), vice chairman. Oversaw Wayne County's paratransit transition and worked as an NCDOT statewide transportation planner. Former teacher and Army veteran.
qual.why: Prior state legislative service and local elected office, plus public-sector management and planning experience, put him in the middle-to-upper part of the range. He has no federal office experience.

cands.bio: Greg Murphy is a Greenville urologist and practice owner. He was a North Carolina House member from 2015 to 2019 and has represented North Carolina's 3rd District in the U.S. House since a September 2019 special election. He serves on the Ways and Means Committee.

controversies.text: Federal records show $27,900 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $36,052 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26; 1 trip paid for by the American Israel Education Foundation, AIPAC's affiliate.
Missed 87 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (12.9%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 61, 2025-12-15 to 2026-01-20.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump (R) endorsed Murphy in the 2026 general election, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We could not find any documented action or statement by Murphy on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign purchases of land, growth and land conservation, school choice or teacher pay, police pay and pensions, or foreign-linked donor refusals. We found no stated position on data centers or development. We found no documented foreign ties. His planks on guns, abortion and immigration rest on a 2019 campaign platform quoted by Ballotpedia, not on current statements. We did not read the current congressional record of his bills. Sources disagree on his birthplace (Raleigh vs. Tarrytown, New York), so we did not report it.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.
